244	class ScanCursor:
245	    """Ordered read-only cursor over one pinned committed snapshot.
246	
247	    Created by :meth:`Store.scan`. Iterating yields ``(key, value)`` pairs
248	    in bytewise key order -- keys ordered by their raw UTF-8 bytes, values
249	    returned as the exact stored bytes -- covering the range given at open:
250	    the start key inclusive, the end key exclusive, either side unbounded
251	    when its endpoint was ``None``.
252	
253	    The snapshot is fully materialised when the cursor opens, so later
254	    commits, compaction, crash recovery or reclamation of the old log space
255	    never change what the cursor yields, and closing the store it came from
256	    does not disturb it. The cursor is an iterator; it is also a context
257	    manager, and ``close()`` releases the snapshot early. Reading from a
258	    closed cursor raises ``ValueError``.
259	
260	    :meth:`token` serialises the current position into an opaque ``bytes``
261	    token naming the pinned snapshot, the scan range and the next position.
262	    ``Store.scan(token=...)`` -- in this process or in a freshly opened
263	    store -- continues the identical scan from that position.
264	    """
265	
266	    def __init__(self, items, lo_idx=0, hi_idx=None, pos=None, seq=0,
267	                 lo=None, hi=None, publisher=None, sid=None, leases=None):
268	        # ``items`` is the materialised snapshot: (key, value) pairs already
269	        # sorted by the keys' raw UTF-8 bytes. The visible window is
270	        # [lo_idx, hi_idx) and the next position starts at ``pos``.
271	        self._items = items
272	        self._lo_idx = lo_idx
273	        self._hi_idx = len(items) if hi_idx is None else hi_idx
274	        self._pos = lo_idx if pos is None else pos
275	        self._seq = seq
276	        self._lo = lo
277	        self._hi = hi
278	        # Writer-only callback durably publishing the pinned snapshot so a
279	        # minted token survives compaction and reclamation; ``None`` on
280	        # read-only stores, which never create or modify any file.
281	        self._publisher = publisher
282	        self._sid = sid
283	        # An open cursor counts as a user of its snapshot for the
284	        # reclamation rules: its box keeps the snapshot's pin alive in the
285	        # process-wide pin set until ``close()`` (or destruction), so
286	        # reclamation never removes the copy an open cursor is over. The
287	        # content identity is derived lazily on the first token mint, or at
288	        # open when a cross-process lease must be registered with it.
289	        self._box = _register_snapshot(seq, items, sid)
290	        # Every cursor -- opened on a read-only store or on a writer --
291	        # additionally holds a cross-process lease for its pinned snapshot
292	        # (``leases`` is the opening store's lease registry), so a writer in
293	        # *another* process treats the snapshot as in use even after this
294	        # cursor's own store has closed. A read-only cursor's identity is
295	        # already known from the store's open; a writer cursor's is derived
296	        # here, at open, so its registration scope matches a reader's.
297	        self._leases = leases
298	        self._lease_held = False
299	        self._lease_finalizer = None
300	        # Only a snapshot that actually has a published copy (seq >= 1) can
301	        # need cross-process protection.
302	        if leases is not None and seq >= 1:
303	            if sid is None:
304	                sid = _snapshot_id(items)
305	                self._sid = sid
306	                # Share the derived identity with the pin box, exactly as a
307	                # lazy token mint would.
308	                self._box._sid = sid
309	            leases.acquire(seq, sid)
310	            self._lease_held = True
311	            # A cursor dropped without close() must release its lease the way
312	            # its weak in-process pin releases on GC.
313	            self._lease_finalizer = weakref.finalize(
314	                self, _release_lease, leases, seq, sid)
315	        self._closed = False
316	
317	    def __iter__(self) -> "ScanCursor":
318	        return self
319	
320	    def __next__(self):
321	        if self._closed:
322	            raise ValueError("scan cursor is closed")
323	        if self._pos >= self._hi_idx:
324	            raise StopIteration
325	        item = self._items[self._pos]
326	        self._pos += 1
327	        return item
328	
329	    def token(self) -> bytes:
330	        """Serialise the current position into an opaque scan token.
331	
332	        The returned ``bytes`` name the pinned snapshot (its durable
333	        sequence number and content identity), the scan range and the next
334	        position. Feeding the token to ``Store.scan(token=...)`` -- in this
335	        process or in a freshly opened store, writer or read-only -- opens
336	        a cursor that continues the same range from the same position over
337	        the same pinned snapshot, byte-identical to the tail of this scan.
338	
339	        Token bytes are platform-independent and deterministic: the same
340	        snapshot at the same position always mints the same token. On a
341	        writer store minting also publishes the pinned snapshot as an
342	        immutable sidecar so the token survives compaction and reclamation
343	        of the old log space; a read-only store never publishes a snapshot
344	        copy when minting (it only holds the cross-process lease registered
345	        when the cursor opened).
346	        """
347	        if self._closed:
348	            raise ValueError("scan cursor is closed")
349	        if self._sid is None:
350	            self._sid = _snapshot_id(self._items)
351	            # Share the derived identity with the pin box so the in-use
352	            # check at reclamation never hashes this snapshot again.
353	            self._box._sid = self._sid
354	        if self._publisher is not None:
355	            self._publisher(self._seq, self._sid, self._items)
356	        return _encode_token(self._seq, self._sid, self._lo, self._hi,
357	                             self._pos)
358	
359	    def mark(self) -> bytes:
360	        """Alias for :meth:`token`."""
361	        return self.token()
362	
363	    @property
364	    def closed(self) -> bool:
365	        return self._closed
366	
367	    def close(self) -> None:
368	        if self._closed:
369	            return
370	        _unpin_snapshot(self._box)
371	        if self._lease_held:
372	            # Detach the GC finalizer: this explicit release is the one.
373	            if self._lease_finalizer is not None:
374	                self._lease_finalizer.detach()
375	            self._leases.release(self._seq, self._sid)
376	            self._lease_held = False
377	        self._items = []
378	        self._box = None
379	        self._closed = True
380	
381	    def __enter__(self) -> "ScanCursor":
382	        return self
383	
384	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
385	        self.close()

399	_OP_PUT = "p"
400	_OP_DELETE = "d"

420	# Cross-process in-use registration. The in-process pin set only names users

425	# together with a heartbeat timestamp, and is atomically rewritten in place.

427	# every fresh one as an in-use pin. An orderly close removes the file; a
428	# process killed without closing stops heartbeating, so once its timestamp

444	def _snapshot_image(items) -> bytes:
445	    """Canonical byte image of a committed snapshot: one put frame per key.

460	def _encode_token(seq: int, sid: bytes, lo: bytes | None,
461	                  hi: bytes | None, pos: int) -> bytes:
462	    """Serialise a scan position; the exact inverse of :func:`_decode_token`."""
463	    flags = (1 if lo is not None else 0) | (2 if hi is not None else 0)
464	    parts = [_TOKEN_MAGIC, seq.to_bytes(8, "big"), sid, bytes((flags,))]
465	    for bound in (lo, hi):
466	        raw = bound if bound is not None else b""
467	        parts.append(len(raw).to_bytes(4, "big"))
468	        parts.append(raw)
469	    parts.append(pos.to_bytes(8, "big"))
470	    body = b"".join(parts)
471	    return body + zlib.crc32(body).to_bytes(4, "big")

474	def _decode_token(tok: bytes):
475	    """Parse a scan token into ``(seq, sid, lo, hi, pos)``.
476	
477	    Every malformation -- wrong magic, truncation, trailing garbage, a
478	    checksum mismatch, unknown flags, a hidden endpoint or a reversed
479	    range -- raises ``ValueError``; nothing is guessed or repaired.
480	    """
481	    if len(tok) < 4 + 8 + 32 + 1 + 4 + 4 + 8 + 4:
482	        raise ValueError("not a scan token")
483	    if tok[:4] != _TOKEN_MAGIC:
484	        raise ValueError("not a scan token")
485	    if int.from_bytes(tok[-4:], "big") != zlib.crc32(tok[:-4]):
486	        raise ValueError("scan token checksum mismatch")
487	    off = 4
488	    seq = int.from_bytes(tok[off:off + 8], "big")
489	    off += 8
490	    sid = tok[off:off + 32]
491	    off += 32
492	    flags = tok[off]
493	    off += 1
494	    if flags & ~0x03:
495	        raise ValueError("scan token carries unknown flags")
496	    bounds = []
497	    for present in (flags & 1, flags & 2):
498	        if off + 4 > len(tok) - 4:
499	            raise ValueError("scan token is truncated")
500	        size = int.from_bytes(tok[off:off + 4], "big")
501	        off += 4
502	        if off + size > len(tok) - 4:
503	            raise ValueError("scan token is truncated")
504	        if not present and size != 0:
505	            raise ValueError("scan token carries a hidden endpoint")
506	        bounds.append(tok[off:off + size] if present else None)
507	        off += size
508	    if off + 8 != len(tok) - 4:
509	        raise ValueError("scan token length mismatch")
510	    pos = int.from_bytes(tok[off:off + 8], "big")
511	    lo, hi = bounds
512	    if lo is not None and hi is not None and lo > hi:
513	        raise ValueError("scan token range is reversed")
514	    return seq, sid, lo, hi, pos

517	class _SnapshotBox:
518	    """Strong box around one user's materialised, pinned snapshot.

521	    cursor and every read-only store holds its own box for the snapshot it
522	    serves. Boxes live in a process-wide :class:`weakref.WeakSet`, so a
523	    cursor or reader that is garbage collected without an explicit
524	    ``close()`` releases its pin automatically -- the in-use table can
525	    neither leak nor outlive the snapshots it protects. The content
526	    identity is hashed lazily, so a scan that neither mints a token nor
527	    registers a cross-process lease pays no hashing cost.
528	    """

533	        self.seq = seq
534	        self.items = items
535	        self._sid = sid

538	        if self._sid is None:

579	def _pid_alive(pid: int) -> bool:
580	    """Best-effort liveness check for the process a lease sidecar names.
581	
582	    A lease whose owner process no longer exists expires on the spot --
583	    no heartbeat can ever come from it again -- so the writer treats its
584	    records as stale and sweeps the file without waiting out the TTL. Any
585	    doubt (a process owned by another user, an unsupported platform, a
586	    transient error) reads as *alive*: expiring a live holder's lease would
587	    break its protection, while a dead holder's lease also expires by
588	    heartbeat TTL, only later.
589	    """
590	    if pid == os.getpid():
591	        return True
592	    if sys.platform == "win32":  # pragma: no cover - windows only
593	        return _pid_alive_windows(pid)
594	    try:
595	        os.kill(pid, 0)
596	    except ProcessLookupError:
597	        return False
598	    except OSError:
599	        # PermissionError and friends: the process exists but is not ours
600	        # to signal, which is proof enough of life.
601	        return True
602	    return True

605	def _pid_alive_windows(pid: int) -> bool:  # pragma: no cover - windows only
606	    """OpenProcess-based liveness check for Windows.
607	
608	    ``os.kill(pid, 0)`` cannot be used there: any signal value other than
609	    ``CTRL_C_EVENT``/``CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`` terminates the target process.
610	    """
611	    try:
612	        import ctypes
613	        kernel32 = ctypes.windll.kernel32
614	        # PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION.
615	        handle = kernel32.OpenProcess(0x1000, False, pid)
616	        if not handle:
617	            return False
618	        try:
619	            code = ctypes.c_ulong()
620	            if not kernel32.GetExitCodeProcess(handle, ctypes.byref(code)):
621	                return True
622	            return code.value == 259  # STILL_ACTIVE
623	        finally:
624	            kernel32.CloseHandle(handle)
625	    except Exception:
626	        return True

638	    sequence, so a resolution against an unpinned sequence hashes nothing.
639	    """
640	    for box in _PINS:
641	        if box.seq == seq and box.sid() == sid:
642	            return box.items
643	    return None

646	class _LeaseManager:
647	    """Cross-process registry of snapshots currently in use.
648	
649	    A process that opens a read-only store or holds a cursor or resume
650	    session over some snapshot -- on either open form of the store -- owns
651	    exactly one lease sidecar --
652	    ``wal.lease.<pid>.<rand>``, all of the single ``wal.lease.*`` kind --
653	    listing every snapshot that process has in use, one fixed-width
654	    ``wal.l<seq>.<sid>.<heartbeat>\\n`` record each. The file is rewritten
655	    atomically (temp file, rename; no fsync, because a lease need not
656	    survive a crash) on every change and every heartbeat, so another
657	    process never observes a half-written record: what it reads is one
658	    complete lease image or the previous one.
659	
660	    Because each process writes only its own file, registering, refreshing
661	    and removing a lease never races another process's lease. An orderly
662	    ``close()`` deletes the sidecar; a process killed without closing simply
663	    stops heartbeating. Expiry is then detected two ways: the heartbeat
664	    timestamps go stale after the TTL, and a sidecar whose owning process no
665	    longer exists expires immediately -- a dead owner can never heartbeat
666	    again. The writer reads *all* lease sidecars before reclaiming a copy,
667	    so a snapshot a cursor or a read-only store in any process is serving is
668	    never removed.
669	
670	    A lease is a protection, never a requirement: writes are best-effort, so
671	    a read-only directory simply has no sidecar and reading is unaffected,
672	    while the in-process pins still apply.
673	    """
674	
675	    def __init__(self, directory: str):
676	        self._dir = directory
677	        # A unique name per process instance. The random suffix keeps two
678	        # incarnations of one pid (pid reuse, or processes sharing a copied
679	        # directory) from ever touching one sidecar.
680	        self._name = f"{_LEASE_PREFIX}{os.getpid()}.{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
681	        self._path = os.path.join(directory, self._name)
682	        # Snapshot keys this process currently leases, reference counted: a
683	        # read-only store and each of its cursors pin independently, so one
684	        # key stays registered until every holder has released it.
685	        self._counts: dict[tuple[int, bytes], int] = {}
686	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
687	        self._stop = threading.Event()
688	        self._thread = None
689	        self._disabled = False
690	
691	    def __del__(self) -> None:
692	        # Defensive backstop: if a manager is collected while it still lists
693	        # keys (its holders' explicit releases and finalizers normally clear
694	        # these first), drop the sidecar. The daemon heartbeat thread, while
695	        # alive, holds a reference to this manager, so by here it has exited.
696	        try:
697	            if getattr(self, "_counts", None):
698	                self._remove_locked()
699	                self._stop.set()
700	        except Exception:
701	            pass
702	
703	    # -- record format -----------------------------------------------------
704	
705	    @staticmethod
706	    def _record(seq: int, sid: bytes, now: float) -> bytes:
707	        # Microseconds since the epoch as a fixed 16-digit integer: exactly
708	        # 16 digits for every realistic date (no variable-width decimal
709	        # point), so every record is one constant width on every platform.
710	        ts = str(int(now * 1_000_000)).rjust(_LEASE_TS_LEN, "0")[-_LEASE_TS_LEN:]
711	        return (f"{_LEASE_REC_PREFIX}{seq:0{_LEASE_SEQ_MAX}d}."
712	                f"{sid.hex()}.").encode("ascii") + ts.encode("ascii") + b"\n"
713	
714	    def _image(self, now: float) -> bytes:
715	        return b"".join(self._record(seq, sid, now)
716	                        for seq, sid in sorted(self._counts))
717	
718	    def _publish(self, now: float | None = None) -> None:
719	        """Atomically write this process's current lease image.
720	
721	        Temp file plus a rename, deliberately *without* fsync: a lease only
722	        has to be visible to a concurrently running writer, never to survive
723	        a crash -- a crashed owner's lease is treated as stale regardless,
724	        and a machine crash leaves no live owner at all. Skipping the fsync
725	        (and the directory sync) keeps a read-only open and each heartbeat
726	        cheap, while the rename still guarantees the writer reads either the
727	        previous complete image or the new one, never a torn file.
728	        """
729	        if self._disabled:
730	            return
731	        if now is None:
732	            now = time.time()
733	        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
734	        try:
735	            with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
736	                f.write(self._image(now))
737	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
738	        except OSError:
739	            # A read-only directory can never host a lease: stop trying so a
740	            # reader there stays free of repeated failing writes. Any other
741	            # OSError (e.g. a brief Windows rename collision with a concurrent
742	            # reader of the file) is transient -- leave the lease enabled and
743	            # let the next heartbeat republish it, so a live holder is never
744	            # mistaken for a dead one.
745	            if not os.access(self._dir, os.W_OK):
746	                self._disabled = True
747	            try:
748	                os.unlink(tmp)
749	            except OSError:
750	                pass

752	    # -- lease lifecycle ---------------------------------------------------
753	
754	    def acquire(self, seq: int, sid: bytes) -> None:
755	        """Take one reference on the lease for ``(seq, sid)``.
756	
757	        Idempotent across the holders of one process (a read-only store and
758	        each of its cursors): the key is registered once on disk but stays
759	        until every holder has released it.
760	        """
761	        if sid is None or seq < 1:
762	            # The empty initial snapshot (seq 0) never has a published copy
763	            # and so never needs a lease.
764	            return
765	        key = (seq, sid)
766	        with self._lock:
767	            count = self._counts.get(key, 0) + 1
768	            self._counts[key] = count
769	            if count == 1:
770	                self._publish()
771	                self._start_locked()
772	
773	    def release(self, seq: int, sid: bytes) -> None:
774	        """Drop one holder's reference; remove the lease at zero. Best effort."""
775	        if sid is None or seq < 1:
776	            return
777	        key = (seq, sid)
778	        thread = None
779	        with self._lock:
780	            count = self._counts.get(key, 0)
781	            if count == 0:
782	                return
783	            if count > 1:
784	                self._counts[key] = count - 1
785	                self._publish()
786	                return
787	            del self._counts[key]
788	            if self._counts:
789	                self._publish()
790	            else:
791	                self._remove_locked()
792	                thread = self._thread
793	                self._stop.set()
794	                self._thread = None
795	        # Join without holding the lock: a heartbeat already past its wait
796	        # may need the lock for one last publish before observing the stop.
797	        self._join_thread(thread)

799	    def close(self) -> None:
800	        """Retire every lease this manager's holders still hold."""
801	        with self._lock:
802	            self._remove_locked()
803	            self._counts.clear()
804	            thread = self._thread
805	            self._stop.set()
806	            self._thread = None
807	        if thread is not None:
808	            self._join_thread(thread)

810	    def _join_thread(self, thread=None) -> None:
811	        if thread is None:
812	            return
813	        if thread is not threading.current_thread():
814	            thread.join(timeout=_LEASE_HEARTBEAT * 4)

816	    def _remove_locked(self) -> None:
817	        if self._disabled:
818	            return
819	        try:
820	            os.unlink(self._path)

823	        except OSError:
824	            # Left behind only if unwritable: it will expire by heartbeat.

830	        if self._thread is not None or self._disabled:
831	            return

837	    def _run(self) -> None:

845	    @staticmethod
846	    def _parse_record(rec: bytes, now: float):
847	        """Return ``(seq, sid)`` for a fresh record, else ``None``.
848	
849	        Malformed bytes, a bad sequence/identity field or a stale heartbeat
850	        all mean "no live user". Every sidecar is published whole, so the
851	        records parsed are always complete ones -- never a torn read.
852	        """
853	        if len(rec) != _LEASE_REC_LEN or not rec.endswith(b"\n"):
854	            return None
855	        try:
856	            text = rec.decode("ascii")
857	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
858	            return None
859	        if not text.startswith(_LEASE_REC_PREFIX):
860	            return None
861	        # Fixed-width layout after "wal.l": seq(20) "." sid(64) "." ts(16).
862	        body = text[len(_LEASE_REC_PREFIX):]
863	        seq_field = body[:_LEASE_SEQ_MAX]
864	        dot1 = body[_LEASE_SEQ_MAX:_LEASE_SEQ_MAX + 1]
865	        sid_field = body[_LEASE_SEQ_MAX + 1:_LEASE_SEQ_MAX + 1 + _LEASE_SID_HEX]
866	        dot2 = body[_LEASE_SEQ_MAX + 1 + _LEASE_SID_HEX:
867	                    _LEASE_SEQ_MAX + 2 + _LEASE_SID_HEX]
868	        ts_field = body[_LEASE_SEQ_MAX + 2 + _LEASE_SID_HEX:
869	                        _LEASE_SEQ_MAX + 2 + _LEASE_SID_HEX + _LEASE_TS_LEN]
870	        if dot1 != "." or dot2 != ".":
871	            return None
872	        try:
873	            seq = int(seq_field)
874	            sid = bytes.fromhex(sid_field)
875	            micros = int(ts_field)
876	        except ValueError:
877	            return None
878	        if len(sid) != 32 or seq < 1:
879	            return None
880	        if now - micros / 1_000_000 > _LEASE_TTL:
881	            return None
882	        return seq, sid

951	    def prune(self, now: float | None = None) -> None:

954	        A sidecar whose every record is stale or malformed belongs to a
955	        process that ended without closing (its heartbeat stopped) and is
956	        swept, as is any sidecar whose owning process no longer exists --
957	        exit detection expires it ahead of the heartbeat TTL. A sidecar
958	        with at least one fresh record from a live owner is left untouched.
959	        Each unlink is independent, so a kill mid-sweep simply finishes on
960	        the next reclaim. This process's own sidecar is never pruned while
961	        it holds keys.

988	# one directory in this process (and their cursors and resume sessions)
989	# share a manager and therefore one lease sidecar, so independently closing
990	# stores and cursors reference-count the same on-disk records. A manager

1097	def _iter_frames(f):
1098	    """Scan an open binary log file from position 0.
1099	
1100	    For every intact frame yields
1101	    ``("frame", meta, value, start, end)``. Scanning stops with either no
1102	    terminal event (clean EOF), ``("torn", start)`` for a single incomplete
1103	    final frame, or ``("invalid", start)`` for a frame that fails framing,
1104	    header/payload checksum or metadata parsing. With the header checksum a
1105	    partial header that borrows bytes from a following record cannot survive,
1106	    so a short read landing exactly at EOF is reliably the one unfinished
1107	    record a single writer was appending when it died; bytes left beyond such
1108	    a read instead make it corruption.
1109	    """
1110	    f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
1111	    eof = f.tell()
1112	    f.seek(0)
1113	    while True:
1114	        start = f.tell()
1115	        header = f.read(_HEADER)
1116	        if not header:
1117	            return
1118	        if len(header) < _HEADER:
1119	            # Trailing bytes of a frame header are a torn tail only when
1120	            # nothing follows them; a gap anywhere else is corruption.
1121	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
1122	                   else ("invalid", start))
1123	            return
1124	        if header[:4] != _MAGIC:
1125	            yield "invalid", start
1126	            return
1127	        if int.from_bytes(header[_PREFIX:], "big") != zlib.crc32(
1128	                header[:_PREFIX]):
1129	            yield "invalid", start
1130	            return
1131	        length = int.from_bytes(header[4:_PREFIX], "big")
1132	        if length > _MAX_PAYLOAD:
1133	            yield "invalid", start
1134	            return
1135	        payload = f.read(length)
1136	        checksum = f.read(_TRAILER)
1137	        if len(payload) < length or len(checksum) < _TRAILER:
1138	            # Only the single final record may be incomplete.
1139	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
1140	                   else ("invalid", start))
1141	            return
1142	        if int.from_bytes(checksum, "big") != zlib.crc32(payload):
1143	            yield "invalid", start
1144	            return
1145	        newline = payload.find(b"\n")
1146	        if newline < 0:
1147	            yield "invalid", start
1148	            return
1149	        try:
1150	            meta = json.loads(payload[:newline])
1151	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
1152	            yield "invalid", start
1153	            return
1154	        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not isinstance(meta.get("t"), str):
1155	            yield "invalid", start
1156	            return
1157	        yield "frame", meta, payload[newline + 1:], start, f.tell()

1195	def inject_tear(source, destination, offset):
1196	    """Copy a log cut at exactly ``offset`` bytes, for bytewise verification.
1197	
1198	    Produces ``destination`` containing the first ``offset`` bytes of
1199	    ``source`` -- a replica of a process killed precisely when the write had
1200	    reached that byte offset. The source file is never modified. Either path
1201	    argument may be a store directory, in which case its ``wal.log`` is used.
1202	
1203	    ``offset`` must satisfy ``0 <= offset <= len(source)``; a negative or
1204	    past-the-end offset raises ``IndexError``. The full-length copy
1205	    (``offset == len(source)``) is the clean control case.
1206	
1207	    Verification aid only; the normal write path never calls this.
1208	    """
1209	    if not isinstance(offset, int) or isinstance(offset, bool):
1210	        raise TypeError("offset must be an integer byte offset")
1211	
1212	    src = os.path.join(source, LOG_NAME) if os.path.isdir(source) else source
1213	    dst = (os.path.join(destination, LOG_NAME)
1214	           if os.path.isdir(destination) else destination)
1215	
1216	    size = os.path.getsize(src)
1217	    if offset < 0 or offset > size:
1218	        raise IndexError(
1219	            f"tear offset {offset} out of range for log of {size} bytes")
1220	    if os.path.abspath(src) == os.path.abspath(dst):
1221	        raise ValueError("tear destination must differ from the source log")
1222	
1223	    remaining = offset
1224	    with open(src, "rb") as fsrc, open(dst, "wb") as fdst:
1225	        while remaining:
1226	            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
1227	            if not chunk:  # pragma: no cover - size came from the same file
1228	                raise IndexError("source log shrank while copying")
1229	            fdst.write(chunk)
1230	            remaining -= len(chunk)
1231	        fdst.truncate(offset)
1232	        os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
